item.title: PostgreSQL 19 reaches GA and is available on Lakebase
item.description:
PostgreSQL 19 reaches GA and is available on Lakebase

PostgreSQL 19 reached general availability today and is already available on Lakebase. Several engineers on the Lakebase team are PostgreSQL committers and contributors who worked on this release directly, from query plan advice to shared memory, locale handling, and release management. New major versions often take weeks to reach other managed PostgreSQL services.

🔍 Overview

PostgreSQL 19 is a practical release with no single headline feature that changes what PostgreSQL is. Instead, version 19 goes after operational problems that database teams know well:

  • Bloated tables
  • Unstable query plans
  • Replica lag
  • Incomplete statistics
  • Maintenance work that is hard to run safely in production

🧩 Key Features

  • REPACK — reclaims space while normal reads and writes continue during most of the operation
  • pg_plan_advice — describes planner decisions as advice, applies supplied advice, and reports whether it was followed
  • pg_stash_advice — stores advice by query ID and applies it automatically when a matching query is planned

⚙️ How REPACK Works

PostgreSQL uses multiversion concurrency control, so an UPDATE creates a new row version and a DELETE leaves a dead tuple behind. Routine vacuuming makes that space reusable, but it doesn’t necessarily return space to the operating system or restore a useful physical row order. The usual fixes — VACUUM FULL, CLUSTER, or external tools such as pg_repack — take an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the whole operation, blocking normal access to the table.

REPACK reclaims space like VACUUM FULL; with USING INDEX, it also physically orders rows like CLUSTER. With CONCURRENTLY, PostgreSQL rebuilds the table while normal reads and writes continue, capturing ongoing changes through logical decoding. It then takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock to apply any remaining captured changes and swap the new table and index files into place.

Component Role
pg_plan_advice Describes planner decisions as advice, applies supplied advice, reports whether it was followed
pg_stash_advice Stores advice by query ID and applies it automatically when a matching query is planned

These components do not add cross-table statistics or replace the planner. Instead, they let you intervene when an inaccurate estimate produces a poor plan. Unlike inline optimizer hints, plan advice lives outside the application’s query text. You can inspect the current plan, test focused advice, and then stash it by query ID.

⚠️ REPACK Limitations

Concurrent repacking creates an additional replication slot for the duration of the operation, so it needs free capacity under max_repack_replication_slots and a table with either a non-deferrable primary key or a suitable index-based replica identity. It also needs temporary disk space for a copy of the table and all its indexes, potentially plus a sort file up to the size of the table.

Tables with heavy update and delete traffic face an additional limit: the current upstream PostgreSQL 19 implementation fails if more than about 104 million tuples in the target table are updated or deleted while REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) is running. This counts changes made during the repack, not rows already in the table.

Concurrent repacking is also not MVCC-safe: after it commits, transactions using snapshots taken before the repack began can see the table as empty. Physical clustering also degrades as later writes arrive. REPACK CONCURRENTLY still needs planning, but it brings into core a job that previously required more downtime or an extension.

🚀 Availability

To try it, create a new Lakebase project and select PostgreSQL 19 as the version.

#PostgreSQL #Lakebase #Database #GARelease #REPACK #QueryPlanning

Source: PostgreSQL 19 is available on Lakebase

item.title: NornicDB combines graph and vector search with sub-millisecond latency
item.description:
NornicDB combines graph and vector search with sub-millisecond latency

🔍 Overview

NornicDB is a distributed, low-latency database that integrates Graph and Vector capabilities with Temporal MVCC. It is designed to provide sub-millisecond performance for HNSW search, graph traversal, and writes.

🧩 How it works

The system allows users to query connected data using Cypher with compatible Bolt drivers. It supports combining graph traversal with vector and full-text retrieval. Historical state can be modeled using MVCC and retained history.

⚙️ Key details

  • Interfaces: Supports Neo4j Bolt/Cypher and qdrant’s gRPC, allowing switching without changes.
  • Features: Includes schemas, managed embeddings, reranking, LLM integration, GPU acceleration, Auto-TLP, Policy-based Memory Decay, and an MCP server.
  • Architecture: Multi-arch support includes CPU, CUDA, Metal, and Vulkan.
  • Integration: Can be embedded in Go applications and supports HTTP interfaces.

🚀 Availability

NornicDB is available via Docker images and native installers.

Platform Instructions
NVIDIA CUDA Use image timothyswt/nornicdb-amd64-cuda-bge:latest
Vulkan Use image timothyswt/nornicdb-amd64-vulkan-bge:latest
macOS Docker does not expose Metal acceleration; native install or local build required for GPU acceleration. Download .pkg installer (arm64 for Apple Silicon, amd64 for Intel) or use Homebrew.
Windows Run .\bin\nornicdb.exe serve

Users can access the admin UI at http://localhost:7474. Benchmark results depend on workload and hardware.

#GraphDatabase #VectorSearch #Cypher #NornicDB #GoLang

Source: orneryd/NornicDB

item.title: Study: Hyperscale Data Centers in US Emit 25.7 Million Tons of CO2
item.description:
Study: Hyperscale Data Centers in US Emit 25.7 Million Tons of CO2

A new paper published in the journal Nature Sustainability reveals that fossil fuels remain the biggest source of electricity for hyperscale data centers in the US, resulting in significant greenhouse gas emissions.

🔍 Overview

The study focuses on hyperscale facilities—massive structures spanning millions of square feet built largely to support generative AI. Researchers from the team of Guidi used satellite imagery to identify 403 hyperscale data centers in the US, estimating each facility’s power consumption based on its electrical capacity. Using data from the Environmental Protection Agency, they approximated carbon pollution for the period between May 2024 and April 2025.

⚙️ Key details

  • Total Consumption: The 403 facilities likely consumed around 82 terawatt-hours of electricity, representing about 1.8 percent of all US electricity consumption.
  • Emissions: Electricity demand from these centers produced 25.7 million metric tons of CO2 emissions.
  • Global Comparison: This consumption level exceeds the individual electricity burn of about 148 nations, and the emissions exceed the total carbon emissions of about 113 nations.
  • Energy Source: About 54 percent of the electricity consumed likely came from gas and coal.
  • Regional Variance: The study showed how the local electricity mix impacts environmental outcomes; for example, generating electricity in coal-reliant Wyoming led to roughly seven times more carbon emissions per kilowatt-hour than in hydropower-rich Oregon.

💡 Why it matters

Fengqi You, a professor in energy systems engineering at Cornell University, states that the results highlight the problem of “long-term carbon lock-in,” noting that power plants built to meet demand may operate for decades and shape emissions well into the future. Both You and Guidi pointed out that researchers had to use satellite imagery to estimate energy consumption because data center operators do not disclose that information. To address this, Guidi and his colleagues are using their research to build a website to track the environmental impact of individual data centers, while a bipartisan bill in Congress aims to mandate greater disclosures nationally.

#DataCenters #Sustainability #AI #Climate

Source: US data centers now burn more electricity than a midsized country

item.title: EmbeddingGemma 2 released under Apache 2.0 license
item.description:
EmbeddingGemma 2 released under Apache 2.0 license

EmbeddingGemma 2, an embedding model, was announced on 6 October 2026 and is licensed under Apache 2.0.

🔍 Overview

  • The model is designed for generating embedding vectors, which are commonly calculated in the thousands or millions and stored for later similarity comparison.
  • Its open‑source Apache 2.0 license means the weights are publicly available for anyone to download and run.

💡 Why it matters

  • Embedding models are often used at scale, so relying on a closed, proprietary, hosted‑only model can create vendor lock‑in risk.
  • If a provider stops offering a proprietary model, users may have to re‑embed all stored vectors, incurring additional cost.
  • An open‑license model lets users switch providers or self‑host later, avoiding that risk.

⚙️ Key details

  • License: Apache 2.0 (open source, permissive).
  • Target use‑case: Large‑scale embedding generation where millions of vectors are stored for later comparison.
  • User preference expressed: Pay a provider for hosted inference while retaining the ability to run the open‑weights version themselves if hosting ends.

🚀 Availability

  • The model’s weights are publicly available under the Apache 2.0 license, allowing anyone to download and run the model independently.
  • Users can still choose a hosted service for convenience, knowing they have a fallback option.

No additional figures are provided.

#EmbeddingGemma #OpenSource #AIEmbeddings #ApacheLicense

item.title: Marvell to Showcase AI Data Center Connectivity and Memory Solutions
item.description:
Marvell to Showcase AI Data Center Connectivity and Memory Solutions

Marvell Technology, Inc. has announced it will present its portfolio of AI data center connectivity and memory solutions at the AI Infra Summit 2026, taking place September 15 to 17 in Santa Clara, California.

⚙️ Key details

Marvell will highlight advances in its end-to-end data center connectivity portfolio for scale-up, scale-out, and scale-across applications at Booth #704. The showcase includes:

Solution Function/Capability
Marvell® Photonic Fabric™ Technology Enables memory sharing across multiple racks, extending scale beyond traditional distance constraints
Marvell RELIANT™ Interconnect Telemetry Platform Provides real-time visibility into the health and performance of AI data center infrastructure connectivity across optical and electrical links
Marvell Teralynx® T100 102 Tbps Ethernet switch device delivering increased bandwidth and efficiency for large-scale AI networks
PCIe 6.0 Switch 256-lane design to connect more accelerators and devices within scale-up AI systems
CXL-based memory solutions Supports expansion, compression, pooling, and near-memory acceleration to reduce dataset movement between XPUs and accelerate large-scale vector databases
DPUs and Ethernet switching Deliver high-performance access to NVMe storage across the network
PCIe® 6.0 NVMe SSD controller Optimized for next-generation enterprise and AI storage

🔍 Overview

During the summit, Marvell executives will participate in panels and presentations regarding connectivity and networking for next-generation AI data center infrastructure. This includes a keynote presentation titled “AI Inference at Scale” delivered by Dave Lazovsky, Executive Vice President and General Manager of the Data Center Networking Business Group.

#Marvell #AIDataCenter #Semiconductors #Networking #AIInfraSummit

Source: Marvell to Showcase End-to-End AI Data Center Connectivity Portfolio at AI Infra Summit 2026
